Hi Markus,

Thanks for the demo last week — FinOptima is moving fast on the procurement side. Before legal signs, we have a few open items in the DPA around incident notification and cooperation with subprocessors:

- Notification window: our security team expects an initial notification within 48 hours of detection with a follow-up timeline for evidence. Can you confirm what Redwood commits to (first alert and sustained updates)?
- Scope: we need clarity on what constitutes a reportable incident under the DPA (unauthorized access, confirmed data exfiltration, privilege misuse).
- Evidence & access: for EU-regulated datasets, we require a limited forensic snapshot and continuity of custody; can Redwood support an evidence handover or escrow for impacted records?
- Cross-border cooperation: how do you handle requests for logs/evidence that touch US-hosted infrastructure and subprocessors? We need the chain-of-custody and transfer controls documented.

Attaching a short spreadsheet with our negotiation points (FinOptima_DPA_questions.xlsx). Can we get proposed contractual language for our procurement team to review?

Hi Lydia — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Marissa (Privacy Ops) to help with precise contract language.

High-level proposals from my side so procurement has something concrete to work with:

1) Initial notification: Redwood will provide an initial alert within 48 hours of confirmed detection or 48 hours of verification of anomalous behavior that indicates potential unauthorized access. The alert will include a preliminary scope, affected customer assets, and mitigation actions in flight.

2) Follow-up cadence: a substantive update within 5 business days with forensic snapshot availability, and subsequent daily updates until containment/closure (or weekly if incident extends beyond 14 days).

3) Evidence handover: Redwood can provide limited forensic exports (read-only snapshot of affected resources, relevant audit logs, and KMS access logs). We will coordinate export packaging with the customer's designated forensic liaison. We prefer to use an approved secure transfer (SFTP or encrypted object key) and can engage a neutral escrow provider for custody if required by the contract.

4) Cross-border transfer: For EU-origin data that requires export, Redwood will: (a) document the transfer path and subprocessors engaged, (b) apply standard SCCs or equivalent, and (c) only transfer minimal artifacts necessary for the investigation. Any transfer to US-hosted subprocessors will be disclosed in the follow-up and logged.

5) Reportable incident definition: We propose to align the DPA to incidents that result in confirmed unauthorized access or exfiltration of Customer Data. Internal operational anomalies that do not impact Customer Data would not trigger the 48-hour DPA window.

I attached a short draft annex with suggested replaceable clauses (DPA_Annex-Notify_Draft_v1.pdf) — Kimberly / Marissa, please review and redline for legal/forensics specifics.

Markus
Head of Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Hi Lydia,

Thanks — I've reviewed Markus's proposals and added legal redlines focused on: scope precision, limited-scope forensic exports, retention/chain-of-custody, and constraints on sharing KMS secrets or raw cryptographic material. High level:

- Narrow the "reportable incident" definition to confirmed unauthorized access to Customer Data, or confirmed exfiltration, to avoid noisy operational alerts triggering contractual windows.
- Forensic snapshots: Redwood will provide a time-bound, read-only snapshot containing application-level records and relevant access logs. We will not provide private keys or KMS secrets; instead we will provide KMS audit logs and signed attestations of snapshot integrity.
- Evidence custody: propose an escrow path where Redwood uploads the snapshot to an agreed SFTP endpoint and retains a signed manifest. If FinOptima requires a neutral custodian, Redwood will coordinate with an approved provider; costs for neutral escrow are to be allocation-based (customer pays third-party escrow fees).
- Cross-border transfers: include an explicit clause that specifies the legal basis (SCCs) and minimum necessary dataset for transfer. Any transfer to US subprocessors will be disclosed within the 5-business-day update and documented with a transfer manifest.

I've attached a marked-up doc (redlines_notify_clause.docx) with exact clause language and a fallback: if a customer requires <24h notification, that becomes an SLA addendum with negotiated credits.

Please review and let us know which parts are non-starters.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
